signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + CB Divergence
signals.text: NZD/JPY remains under intense pressure as the G10 laggard NZD (-1.435% weekly avg) faces the session leader JPY (+1.024% weekly avg). The pair is driven by a stark fundamental divergence: JPY is supported by BoJ Governor Ueda's confirmation that rate hikes remain on the table for September, while NZD is weighed down by an extreme CFTC speculative short position at the 0 percentile of its 52-week range (z -2.60). Despite a 335bp OIS carry advantage for NZD/JPY, the 2.459% bilateral spread reflects a rapid JPY repricing as US 10Y yields stall at 4.80%. Options markets confirm the downside bias with a strong EUR/JPY put skew (RR -1.98), suggesting institutional demand for JPY protection. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY; JPY outperformance theme overrides the nominal carry advantage. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike on the table. Risk: RBNZ Governor Breman’s hawkish inflation warnings trigger a sharp short-squeeze in crowded NZD positions.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD is testing the SMA20 support at 0.7114 after a week of consolidating its recent gains. COT data shows Leveraged Funds are heavily crowded long at the 95th percentile (z +1.92), creating a significant positioning hurdle for further upside. This institutional long-loading is met by extreme retail sentiment, with 86% of retail traders currently short, creating a classic institutional versus retail divergence at a technical pivot. While the 67bp OIS carry premium favors AUD, the stalling 4W flow delta suggests the trend is maturing. A break below the SMA20/50 cluster would likely trigger an unwind of speculative longs towards the SMA200 at 0.6978. Trade bias: Neutral/Range AUD/USD; crowded spec longs limit immediate upside potential. Catalyst: China Private PMI release Thursday. Risk: Retail capitulation leads to a final squeeze higher toward 0.7250.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Volatility Premium + ESI Miss
signals.text: GBP/USD is trading at 1.3488, holding below its SMA20 of 1.3549 as data momentum begins to fade. The pair’s Economic Surprise Index (ESI) has shifted to -9.8, indicating a consistent run of data misses relative to expectations. This fundamental softening is reflected in the options market, where the 1-month ATM IV of 11.0% sits 6.0 points above the 30-day realized volatility of 5.0%. This elevated Vol Risk Premium (VRP) suggests traders are paying a steep premium for protection against a breakdown, likely due to the crowded COT positioning (96th percentile long). With OIS carry effectively neutral at -5bp, the pair lacks a structural yield cushion if the SMA50/200 cluster at 1.3436/43 is tested. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD; elevated vol premium and negative data surprises signal downside risk. Catalyst: BoE meeting 17 Sep — Hold priced. Risk: Positive UK GDP surprise forces an unwind of the 25d RR put skew.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Intervention Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY at 158.71 is navigating a regime shift as BoJ Governor Ueda’s hawkish rhetoric meets a persistent 275bp Fed-BoJ OIS carry advantage. The pair has retreated from the 160.00 level, which previously triggered verbal intervention warnings, and currently sits between its SMA20 (159.12) and SMA200 (158.44). Despite the carry support, the 25d Risk Reversal at -1.82 confirms that the options market is aggressively hedging for JPY strength, contradicting the JPY COT net short of -81,619. VIX at 15.2 indicates normal volatility, suggesting that recent JPY strength is driven by specific policy repricing rather than a broad flight to safety. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; carry advantage is currently offset by BoJ policy pivot risk. Catalyst: Fed meeting 16 Sep — Hike bias. Risk: A break back above 160.16 (Technical close) triggers fresh BoJ verbal warnings.
